annotation.method: Codex extracted and read all 23 pages in physical order, covering Sections 1-6, Theorems 2.1-2.2, Corollaries 2.3-2.4, Lemma 3.1, Algorithms 1-5, every supplied proof and exact operation identity, the numerical example, conclusions, and all 41 references; separated internally proved claims from imported rank-factorization, SVD, compactness, and earlier tensor-rank facts; audited Mathlib and the exact frozen 44-object NumStability surface; and compiled exact private N/L proofs of the strongest no-shortcut candidate before skipping all tiers.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P60 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

corpus_membership: This paper is part of the current corpus listed in metadata/manifest.json.
paper_version: SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 33(5), pages 2295-2317, published electronically 22 September 2011

rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorem 2.1, existence of a tensor-train decomposition from unfolding ranks
rejected_candidates.reason: The proof starts by invoking an exact rank/skeleton factorization and then repeats that construction on auxiliary unfoldings. The paper does not prove the rank-factorization result. Supplying the successive factorizations as hypotheses makes the remaining substitutions short; requiring their construction and the full dependent-dimension induction would add substantial source-external linear-algebra infrastructure rather than isolate the paper's proof. NumStability contains no tensor-train or rank-factorization shortcut.

The proof is presented but the theorem is attributed to [29] and relies on best truncated-SVD properties at every stage. Frozen projection-orthogonality and rectangular Frobenius-isometry results are nearby, but they address only the generic one-step matrix core. The equivalent two-result core was already privately reconstructed in the P58 audit, where L shortened 238 N lines to 198 L lines; all tensor unfolding, reshape, rank, and induction work remains unchanged. That evidence does not establish the much larger T2 advantage required here, and no exact frozen TT-SVD theorem exists.

Corollary 2.3 is an immediate consequence of Theorem 2.2 and an earlier canonical-format observation. Corollary 2.4 additionally uses finite-dimensional subsequence compactness and closedness of bounded-rank unfolding sets; treating those standard assertions as assumptions leaves a short deduction, while rebuilding a full tensor-rank topology development would exceed the proof supplied in the paper.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Lemma 3.1, orthonormality of a contracted train of row-orthonormal cores
rejected_candidates.reason: This is the strongest exact no-shortcut candidate. Exact arbitrary-depth private proofs compile in both conditions in 70 N lines and 71 L lines. Their mathematical bodies are identical, and L uses no NumStability declaration, but the proof is a compact reindexing followed by one induction and repeated matrix-sum factoring. It is well below the required T2-level difficulty and therefore cannot be retained as T3.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Scholes-like tensor rank bound in Section 3.1
rejected_candidates.reason: The source proves the bound by displaying at most k+2 column generators and the analogous row generators. Once those displayed generators are encoded, the remaining span/cardinality argument is standard finite-dimensional linear algebra and below the T3 floor; the broader rank-3 approximation statements used around it are cited from [3].

The addition, contraction, Hadamard-product, dot-product, and matrix-vector formulas are direct distributive or Kronecker-product identities. They have complete source explanations but are too short for the tiers, and their complexity estimates are algorithmic operation counts rather than exact theorem statements.

This is a numerical experiment. The paper explicitly says that verifying the computed value is the smallest eigenvalue remains difficult and under investigation, so no missing correctness theorem may be invented.

T1.decision: Skipped. No exact internally proved P60 result receives one substantial non-Mathlib shortcut from the frozen NumStability bundle.

T2.decision: Skipped. NumStability's projection-orthogonality and Frobenius-isometry results touch only the generic one-step matrix core of Theorem 2.2; prior exact N/L reconstruction of that core shows only a modest reduction, while all tensor-specific work remains. No candidate has the required large two-result advantage.

T3.decision: Skipped. The exact arbitrary-depth Lemma 3.1 candidate is only 70/71 private lines and below the T2 difficulty floor. Harder-looking claims either rely on rank/SVD/topological background not proved in P60, reduce to short span algebra once the paper's displayed decomposition is exposed, or are algorithms and experiments rather than exact proved theorems.

selection_policy: Use only exact claims supported by P60's own statement and proof text.
Do not turn imported rank-factorization, best-SVD, compactness, or earlier tensor-rank results into new P60 proof obligations.
Do not aggregate several easy Section 4 identities into an artificial hard task.
Require the T3 candidate itself, not merely its dependent-index notation, to meet the T2 difficulty floor.
